findings.summary: No link sanitising and no safe mode: javascript:/vbscript:/data: destinations render live
findings.description:
## Affected `github.com/malcolmston/markdown` **<= 0.1.0** (all published versions). No fix released. There is **no public issue** for this finding. Case group `security` (19 cases, `parity/markdown/cases/security.json`). Oracle: `commonmark.js`. ## Read this first: the nuance that determines how to treat this **`commonmark.js` is identically unsafe by default, so this is NOT a regression against upstream.** With its default renderer, upstream produces exactly the same live hrefs for `javascript:` and friends, and 11 of these cases score *at parity*. Being unsafe by default is inherited from the reference implementation, not invented by the port. The actual gap is twofold: 1. **Upstream offers an opt-in sanitiser and the port has no equivalent.** `new HtmlRenderer({safe: true})` blanks unsafe destinations (`

x

`, ``), replaces raw HTML with ``, and leaves benign links untouched. The Go port has no `Options` field, no renderer hook and no exported node-rewriting step that does any of this. All 7 `render_safe` cases are therefore real mismatches, not deviations: `sec-safe-js-scheme-link`, `sec-safe-vbscript-scheme-link`, `sec-safe-data-scheme-link`, `sec-safe-js-scheme-image`, `sec-safe-raw-script-block`, `sec-safe-raw-inline-event-handler`, `sec-safe-http-link-untouched`. 2. **`Options{HTML: false}` is not a sanitiser.** It is the closest thing the port has to a safety switch and it does not do the job: it escapes raw HTML (`opt-nohtml-block`, `opt-nohtml-inline`) but **leaves link destinations completely untouched** - `opt-nohtml-does-not-touch-links` shows `[x](javascript:alert(1))` still rendering ``. Anyone reaching for `HTML: false` expecting safety gets XSS through links. ## Behaviour `DefaultOptions()` in v0.1.0 is `Options{HTML: true, Typographer: false, LineBreaks: false, LinkTarget: ""}` - verified by case `opt-default-options`, which reads the real struct - so raw `
